scenarios.name: husky-to-lefthook-migration
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: it uses `jobs` with glob, {staged_files} and stage_fixed, runs `npx lefthook install`, and verifies with `npx lefthook run pre-commit`. A uses the older `commands` syntax instead of `jobs` and verifies with `--all-files`, so it covers less of the rubric, though it has useful extras like the partial-staging caveat.

scenarios.name: polyglot-monorepo-changed-files-only
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric closely: it installs lefthook without npm, runs `lefthook install`, and uses per-job `root` and `glob` with {staged_files} and stage_fixed, and it explains that a job is skipped when nothing matches; B uses a hand-written Bash hook and the Python pre-commit framework, so it never uses lefthook.

scenarios.name: fix-parallel-race-and-pnpm-hooks
scenarios.rationale: Both show LEFTHOOK=0 and sequential jobs, but B states removing `parallel: true` and puts the pnpm-workspace.yaml `onlyBuiltDependencies` fix front and centre as the install cause, while A relies on `piped: true`, leads with a `prepare` script and buries the workspace fix as a secondary option.
